title: Batch wiring — wiring N ports in one gesture
summary: The feature Zach remembered as "wire within / wire to" is called "Wire into…" and "Wire together" in the donor, it lives in an UNCOMMITTED SystemSketch worktree, and its "smart detection" is one function: the set of dots where a click would actually create cables. Ported as pure scene functions, demonstrated as a driveable DOM Canvas story, and two real bugs found on the way.
branch_label: batch-wiring lane (isolated worktree, cut from the lane tip)
changes: apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/batchWire.ts — new, 0 deps: resolveWirePair, planBatchWire, batchWireTargets (THE availability answer), batchWireSources, batchWireEdges, applyBatchWire, describeBatchWireOutcome. Pure, no React, no engine. Availability rules arrive as an INJECTED WireJudge so this lane and the validateConnection lane compose instead of colliding.

apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/batchWire.standIn.ts — new: a clearly-labelled STAND-IN availability predicate (6 of the donor's 8 refusal reasons over real host port data), to be DELETED when edgeValidation.ts lands. Its own header says so.
apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/batchWire.test.ts — new: 40 pure tests, structure ported from the donor's own 474-line suite.

apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/BatchWiring.stories.tsx — new: Blocks/Scene/Batch Wiring. One driveable Bench plus 5 play-function stories that assert the availability filtering by measured getComputedStyle.

docs/capture_batch_wiring_shots.mjs — new: drives the real bench on real Chromium and shoots BETWEEN the clicks, because an interaction's evidence is a sequence and the existing capture script screenshots a story as it loads.
docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md — appended two rows (batchWire.ts, batchWire.standIn.ts), including the fact that the donor cannot be pinned to a rev.
docs/lane_report_manifest.batch-wiring.json — this file, the input to this report.

NOT touched: src/components/**, src/hosts/**, src/scene/scene.ts, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml. The paint reaches real dots through the repo's own data-block-id/data-port-id DOM contract instead of a component or host edit.
findings: WHAT THE FEATURE ACTUALLY WAS — two commands over ONE mechanism, differing in exactly where a landing click may land. "Wire into…": select sources, invoke, click one dot ANYWHERE a source could legally reach, outside the selection included. "Wire together": select the group, invoke, click one of THEIR OWN ports to elect it the hub; the rest fan into it. Donor batchWiring.ts:1-30, its own header.

ZACH'S NAMES ARE CLOSE BUT NOT THE CODE'S. "wire to" ≈ "Wire into…"; "wire within" ≈ "Wire together". His hedge ("I think two things") was right about the count. "within" also names a real SECOND axis he may have been half-remembering: selecting one CONTAINER is the deliberate shorthand for wiring its members (getWireIntoSources, donor :350-366). Both axes are implemented and switchable.

THE DONOR IS NOT COMMITTED ANYWHERE. batchWiring.ts, batchWiringCommands.ts, wireIntoState.ts, batchWiring.test.ts and SelectionWiringActions.tsx are all `??` untracked in ONE systemsketch worktree (.claude/worktrees/vision-consolidated, branch claude/vision-consolidated). `git log --all -- src/blocks/connections/batchWiring.ts` returns nothing, and the files are absent from src/blocks/connections/ at the donor root. 1,182 lines of working, reviewed feature that a `git stash -u` or `git clean -fd` in that worktree would destroy. Flagged as a preservation risk, not just a citation problem.

THE "SMART DETECTION" IS ONE FUNCTION, and its subtlety is the reason it works: a dot earns its ring only when at least one SOURCE — not merely one PORT — would get a cable. A landing every source resolves ambiguously against is perfectly legal and still wires nothing, so judging per port would make the ring promise landings that then did nothing. Donor's own words, portState.ts:40-56.

"HIDE THE ONES THAT WEREN'T AVAILABLE" IS A DIM, NOT A HIDE — opacity 0.18, and it is a settled value, not a default: Zach reviewed five live-CSS treatments against the running donor on 2026-09-06 and picked Dim (86/100) over Vanish at 0% (84/100) because it keeps the board recognisable while armed. The donor's CSS carries a do-not-retune comment (block-canvas.css:1029-1037). This app's own Port `dimmed` prop paints 0.45 instead (port.tsx:163) — a real, unresolved discrepancy, so the story makes all three switchable with the donor's value as default rather than silently picking one.

A BATCH MAY NOT GUESS. resolveWirePair: an exact port-NAME match wins; failing that, exactly one legal pairing wins; anything else is refused as `ambiguous`. "First port that fits" — fine for a single drag — would quietly wire `config` five times when the user meant `logs`, and a batch's whole value is that you do NOT inspect the forty cables it made (donor :127-147).

BUG FOUND AND FIXED #1 — incremental judging. My first commit re-judged every pair against the same frozen scene, so three sources wired into ONE single-feed input produced three cables and reported no refusals. The donor never had this because judgeConnection reads a live tldraw Editor that editor.run() is mutating as each shape is created; a pure function has to rebuild the scene between pairs. Fixed by making the commit-time judge a FACTORY (SceneJudge) and pinned by a regression test that asserts BOTH halves — the fix, and that a scene-pinned judge still wires all three.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED #2 — backwards edges. batchWireEdges wrote the edge in GESTURE order, not dataflow order. A name match between one block's `logs` INPUT and another's `logs` OUTPUT is a legal pair whose cable must run output → input; it came out reversed, which would have inverted its arrowhead and every producersOf/consumersOf/topologicalOrder read of it. The donor fixes this with normalizeConnectionDirection (donor :330) — a line that reads like tldraw binding plumbing and is in fact this rule. Fixed by having the verdict report the oriented pair, matching the donor's judge, whose ConnectionVerdict already carries explicit source/sink endpoints (connectionRules.ts:53-63).

BOTH BUGS WERE FOUND BY A STORY ASSERTION I HAD WRITTEN WRONG, not by reading the code. The second one surfaced because I asserted that probe/logs could not possibly be available and the suite disagreed; chasing the "wrong" ring found the reversed edge. Both wrong expectations are left recorded in the test/story comments rather than quietly corrected.

MY OWN BASELINE MEASUREMENT WAS CONTAMINATED, and it is worth knowing about. Running `pnpm test-stories` with no STORYBOOK_PORT set probes :5421 — Zach's live review server — so my first baseline reported `1 failed | 216 passed` for a DragPolicy story that has nothing to do with this lane. Re-run on my own port 5498 it passes 9/9 and imports nothing of mine. The true baseline is 50 files / 217 tests green; the single "failure" was this lane's harness testing a different worktree's source, exactly the hazard vitest.config.ts:9-21 already warns about in a comment.

SEAM I WANT FROM THE VALIDATION LANE: their ok-verdict should carry the ORIENTED pair, not just `ok` — otherwise every consumer has to re-derive polarity to avoid writing a backwards edge, and the donor's own judge already reports it. Adapter needed is one line either way: `const judgeFor: SceneJudge = (s) => (c) => validateConnection(s, c);`

COULD NOT VERIFY: the donor's THREE command surfaces (context menu BlockContextMenu.tsx:707, selection toolbar SelectionWiringActions.tsx, command palette) behind one getSelectionWiringAvailability read — I read the files but this app has none of those surfaces, so the "cannot drift apart" property is not reproduced, only recorded. Also not ported: the donor's toast host (the on-canvas read-out stands in for it) and the pending-state tool node (wireIntoState.ts's StateNode is a tldraw select-tool child; the story holds the armed flag in React state instead).
pyblocks checked as Zach suggested: /home/bam/pyblocks has NO batch-wiring vocabulary at all. SystemSketch is the only donor.

stories.title: Batch Wiring · Bench (drive this one)
stories.look_for: Click two or more blocks, pick an intent, press Arm, then click a ringing dot. Switch the `ineligible` control between Dim 18% / Dim 45% / Vanish 0% while armed to compare the treatments on the same board. The `stand-in rules` checkboxes change which dots are available, live.

stories.title: Batch Wiring · Availability Is Filtered
stories.look_for: The mechanical proof. Asserts the exact 6-dot available set, that every ringing dot measures opacity 1, that a named list of unavailable dots measures < 1, and that one real dot measures 0.18 — the donor's frozen value. Ends committed, with the refusal sentence.

stories.title: Batch Wiring · Together Rings Only Its Own Group
stories.look_for: The one line separating the two commands, measured: same selection, same rules, same judge, and "together" drops every dot outside the selection from the ring.

stories.title: Batch Wiring · Ambiguity Is Refused Not Guessed
stories.look_for: A landing that resolves by NAME wires; the same shape with no name to match on refuses `ambiguous` rather than picking one of three legal ports.

stories.title: Batch Wiring · Empty Ring Refuses To Arm
stories.look_for: An armed mode with no affordance is a failure to report, not a mode to sit in. Also: a press away from every ringing dot is a decline, not an error.

stories.title: Batch Wiring · Rules Change Availability
stories.look_for: Availability is a function of the RULES, not the board alone — turning single-feed off puts a dot back in the ring with no re-arm. This is the injected-judge seam made visible.

sections.heading: The gesture, mid-flight
sections.html: Every still below is shot from the same Bench story a human drives, on real Chromium, between the clicks — docs/capture_batch_wiring_shots.mjs. None is a mock and none is a play function's end state. Read 03 against 05: same board, same rules, one control changed, and the ring narrows from the whole board to the selection's own dots. That difference is the difference between the two commands.

images.title: 02 — three sensors selected, nothing armed
images.caption: Selection alone paints nothing off the table. Arming is a separate, explicit step — the donor refuses to enter it at all if the ring would be empty.

images.title: 03 — ARMED, "Wire into…" · available: 6
images.caption: The answer to Zach's question. Six dots ring; every other dot AND its label sit at 18%. Note what is dimmed: the three selected sensors' own outputs, fuse/out, gain/val, and all of probe — all sources, none of which can take a cable. The dots are not gone, so the board stays readable.

images.title: 04 — committed · "Wired 1 cable · skipped 2 input already fed"
images.caption: One real wire, arrowhead pointing AT the input, both endpoints flipped to the `wired` state by the kit's own withWiredState. The other two sources were refused because single-feed caps that input at one producer — and the sentence says so rather than going silent. This is the case that caught bug #1: before the fix it read "Wired 3 cables" with no refusals.

images.title: 05 — ARMED, "Wire together" · available: 3
images.caption: Same three-node selection (cam, lidar, fuse), one control changed. sink/in, sink/logs and gain/set were available a moment ago and are now off the table, because a landing must belong to the armed group. Whichever of fuse's dots is clicked becomes the hub — there is no separate hub concept in the code, here or in the donor.

images.title: 06 — hub elected · "Wired 1 cable into fuse · skipped 1 input already fed"
images.caption: Only "Wire together" names a hub in its sentence, because only it CHOSE that end — donor :456-462.

images.title: 07 — the same armed state at Vanish (0%), for comparison
images.caption: Zach's second-placed treatment, 84/100 against Dim's 86. Worth seeing why it lost: the blocks lose their dots entirely, so cam, lidar, imu and probe stop being recognisable as port-bearing things at all. The story keeps this switchable rather than arguing about it.

sections.heading: The availability predicate I want at the seam
sections.html:
A sibling lane owns the real rules. This lane owns the gesture, and it asks exactly one question, injected — the same way findDanglingEdges takes portsOf (scene.ts:424):

export type WireJudge = (candidate: { source: PortRef; target: PortRef }) => WireVerdict;

export type WireVerdict =
  | { ok: true;  oriented?: { source: PortRef; target: PortRef } }
  | { ok: false; reason: string; silent?: boolean };

// Rebuilt per cable, so cable N is judged against cables 1..N-1:
export type SceneJudge = (scene: BlockScene) => WireJudge;

Three deliberate choices, each one earned by something that went wrong:

  • reason is an opaque string, not a closed union. The precedence order and the human words default to the donor's eight, but they are parameters. A union declared here would force the validation lane to either duplicate the taxonomy or adopt the donor's exact spelling.
  • silent carries your three-valued refusal through unchanged. A silent refusal still removes the dot from the ring — availability is binary — but is left out of the reported tally, so "refused silently" stays silent in the sentence.
  • oriented is the ask. Please have your ok-verdict report the pair ordered by dataflow. Without it every caller re-derives polarity to avoid writing a backwards edge, which is bug #2 above; and your judge already computes polarity, exactly as the donor's does (ConnectionVerdict carries explicit source/sink, connectionRules.ts:53-63).

Adapting validateConnection(scene, candidate) is one line, and batchWire.standIn.ts is then deleted with nothing in batchWire.ts changing:

const judgeFor: SceneJudge = (s) => (c) => validateConnection(s, c);

sections.heading: Where it lived, and the thing to do about it
sections.html:
The donor is five files totalling 1,182 lines, all of them untracked in a single systemsketch worktree:

/home/bam/systemsketch/.claude/worktrees/vision-consolidated/
  src/blocks/connections/batchWiring.ts          473 lines  ??
  src/blocks/connections/batchWiring.test.ts     474 lines  ??
  src/blocks/connections/wireIntoState.ts        164 lines  ??
  src/blocks/connections/batchWiringCommands.ts   71 lines  ??
  src/chrome/SelectionWiringActions.tsx           79 lines  ??

git log --all for those paths returns nothing, and they are absent from src/blocks/connections/ at the donor root — so this feature has never been committed to systemsketch on any branch. Its supporting edits (the opacity: 0.18 CSS, the Port_eligible paint, installConnections.ts' registration of the pending state) sit as M modifications in the same dirty tree.

This is the risk worth naming: per this repo's own CLAUDE.md, a session switching branches in a shared checkout runs git stash -u, and that takes every untracked file with it — which is exactly how a report went missing on 2026-09-15. A git clean -fd in that worktree would be worse. Committing that lane, or listing those paths in its .git/info/exclude, is cheap insurance on a reviewed feature nobody can currently recover from git.

I did not touch it. It is read-only by instruction and I only opened files.
